title: Grain Marketing Contracts: Buying Out the Undelivered Balance of a Contract
content:
Where a member on Grain Marketing Contracts will not deliver bushels they have sold, the contract is closed out against a charge. The result governed is the charge the member pays to be released from the undelivered bushels, booked as a line on the member's grain ledger.

A contract is closed out only by the member's own hand: the member puts the buyout through themselves, and no instruction the member has lodged with the grain desk for another purpose stands as authority to close a contract out.

The buyout charge is struck only after the last day of the contract's delivery window falls later than the day the contract is closed out, with the bushels the contract commits standing as the same written change leaves them.

**Capability.** The call closes the contract out: it books the buyout charge as a line on the member's grain ledger, moves the contract into cancelled standing, stamps today's date as the day it closed and takes the bushels still owed to zero, so no further delivery is expected and no default arises on it. On success the member's records show the contract closed with that charge standing against it.

**How it is invoked, and by whom.** The recorded act is `execute_contract_buyout_11de6ced`. Walking away from bushels the member has sold is the member's own act, so it is not the desk's to perform: the grain desk unlocks it and hands it over, and it is run by the customer themselves, the member in person.

**The parameters it takes.**

- `contract_id` — the internal reference of the grain marketing contract being bought out; it identifies one contract record and is reachable from the grain contract lookup for the member before this call.
- `customer_id` — the internal reference of the member buying the contract out; it identifies one membership record and is reachable from the membership profile lookup before this call.
- `buyout_charge_usd` — the charge the member pays to be released from the undelivered bushels, in USD to 2 decimal places, as a positive number with no currency symbol and no thousands separator, rounded half away from zero at the cent when a longer value is supplied.

**What comes back.** A single confirmation sentence in plain text naming the ledger line reference minted for the buyout charge, the contract that was closed out, and the amount charged in USD to 2 decimal places; that sentence, rather than an error text, is what indicates the contract is bought out.
